headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: open-webui’s persistent shared sessions plus next-ai-draw-io’s broad network/MCP/browser access create a default pathway for sensitive document content to flow into external tools and be…

A_prompt_injection.rationale: next-ai-draw-io ingests PDFs/text/images and uses MCP plus browser/network egress, while open-webui exposes MCP, plugins, and persistent shared sessions. That creates a plausible default bridge where attacker-controlled document content can be surfaced into open-webui prompts or tools. The interaction is documented by both profiles, but not directly reproduced, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF next-ai-draw-io forwards document text into open-webui prompts or MCP tools
IF open-webui processes that content as instructions rather than untrusted data
IF both agents share a workspace, clipboard, or MCP endpoint
mitigations: Disable MCP between the two agents for untrusted documents
Route document text through a sanitizer that strips instructions
Use separate sessions and separate workspaces
Add a fixed prompt prefix that treats imported content as data only
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all cross-agent content

B_data_leakage.rationale: next-ai-draw-io handles PDFs, text files, images, and API keys, and has broad network egress; open-webui stores documents, notes, persistent memory, files, and API keys in persistent shared sessions. If they share files or a mounted workspace, sensitive document content can flow into open-webui and then out through its APIs or plugins. The default blast radius includes exfiltration and secret exposure.
conditions: IF both agents can read the same local files or mounted volume
IF next-ai-draw-io processes documents containing secrets or regulated data
IF open-webui sends those contents to external APIs, search tools, or memory storage
mitigations: Separate the agents onto different volumes
Remove secrets from shared documents before processing
Disable external API/tool calls in open-webui for sensitive sessions
Use offline mode for open-webui when handling confidential files
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage isolation and DLP checks

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have broad network egress and browser access, and open-webui also supports subprocesses plus persistent shared state. next-ai-draw-io can use MCP and elevated environment variables, so concurrent writes or tool actions against shared resources can race or overwrite each other. Because both profiles support multiple instances and no locking is documented, the safer choice is high.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same filesystem, git repo, or mounted data volume
IF open-webui subprocesses or tools mutate shared artifacts
IF next-ai-draw-io writes diagrams while open-webui reads or rewrites the same files
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate working directory
Disable concurrent writes to shared artifacts
Serialize edits with a manual lock file
Run one agent read-only during the other's write phase
requires-engineering: add transactional locking around shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: next-ai-draw-io produces AI-assisted visualizations from documents, and open-webui is a general LLM UI that can route outputs into tools, plugins, or persistent memory. If open-webui treats next-ai-draw-io output as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream actions or stored knowledge. The pathway exists in default configurations and can affect multiple work products.
conditions: IF open-webui uses next-ai-draw-io output as input to tools, memory, or generated responses
IF no human verification step is inserted between agents
IF downstream actions are triggered from the derived content
mitigations: Require human review before any downstream action
Mark next-ai-draw-io output as untrusted in open-webui
Disable auto-save to memory for imported content
Use a verification checklist for extracted facts
requires-engineering: add confidence/provenance gating before tool execution

E_compliance.rationale: Both agents are open-source and docs-only, but open-webui explicitly stores persistent memory, analytics, files, and API keys, while next-ai-draw-io handles documents and secrets. That creates a plausible retention and residency mismatch if regulated documents are processed through open-webui’s persistent storage. The other agent is cited because the risk arises from the pairwise data flow.
conditions: IF regulated or EU personal data is processed through open-webui persistent memory or files
IF retention settings differ between the two agents
IF exported artifacts are stored longer than the source documents
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data into persistent memory
Set short retention on open-webui artifacts
Delete imported files after processing
Document the data flow and residency for both agents
requires-engineering: align retention and deletion policies across both systems
